text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.
LONDON - UK shares soared to a record peak on Tuesday, taking their cue from a resumption of the strong rally on Wall Street.

The FTSE 100 index swept past the key psychological resistance point of 4,700 to close up 52.9 points at 4,739.6, breaking the previous closing and intraday peaks set on May 16. Trading volume was around 800 million shares.
FRANKFURT - A more stable day on the currency markets helped calm the German share market as the blue chip DAX index recouped early losses to end the floor session little changed.

The 30-share DAX closed bourse trade down 2.42 points at 3,665.01 points, having dipped as low as low as 3,648.45 early in the session. In post-bourse trade the index stood at 3,671.16 up 2.55 points.

PARIS - The CAC 40 index closed lower in relatively light volume as investors took their cue from uncertainty over the euro to book profits. Traders said the market needed to consolidate after the surprise rise since the Socialist election win. The bourse shrugged off Wall Street's attack on the 7,500 level and London's record high.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 22.02 points or 0.82 percent at 2,664.18.

ZURICH - After posting five record closes in a row, shares ended marginally lower in what was described as a welcome consolidation. One dealer said sentiment continued to be favourable due to sound fundamentals such as the dollar's strength and a positive interest rate outlook. The blue-chip SMI ended lower by 6.9 points or 0.13 percent at 5,361.9 points. The all-share SPI lost 1.86 points or 0.05 percent to 3,391.34.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed moderately higher as participants were relieved by a stable yen after its sudden surge hammered the key stock index lower on Monday.
The Nikkei 225 average climbed 308.73 points, or 1.53 percent, to close at 20,532.55. Its June futures ended 330 points higher at 20,600.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed sharply lower after heavy profit-taking undid 200 points of initial gains.
The Hang Seng Index dropped 215.42 points, or 1.47 percent, to finish at 14,439.71 after retreating from an early high of 14,856.77.
SYDNEY - A bullish Australian stock market bolted to a record close, capturing an intra-day high along the way as the local market played catch-up with soaring U.S. markets.

The All Ordinaries Index climbed 28 points to a close of 2,628.9, surpassing the previous record close of 2,625.7 reached on June 2. Earlier in the day the market hit an intra-day high of 2,631.3, topping the previous high of 2,626.0.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended weaker but off earlier lows, weighed by worries over the rand's recent slide. Institutional buying offered some support before close after profit-taking hit the market through most of the day. Gold shares ended soft on the back of a dull bullion price.
The industrial index was last down 17.8 points at 8,501.4 points, the gold index was off 4.2 points to 1,777.1 points and the all-share index fell 31.0 points to 7,265.5 points.
